title: "Configuration"
description: "ipmideck reads data/config.yaml and accepts IPMIDECK_-prefixed environment overrides."

## config.yaml

ipmideck reads its settings from `data/config.yaml`, written with sensible defaults on the
first run. You can edit the file directly, or override any value at runtime with an
environment variable (handy for Docker, see below).

```yaml
# data/config.yaml (auto-generated on first run)
server:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 3000
  https: false
auth:
  session_expiry: 24h
ipmi:
  poll_interval: 30
  power_poll_interval: 30
  command_timeout: 30
data:
  retention_days: 365
logging:
  level: info
updates:
  enabled: true
modules:
  sensors:
    enabled: true
  fanpilot:
    enabled: true
  power:
    enabled: true
  sel:
    enabled: true
  fru:
    enabled: true
```

The keys above are the real, unprefixed nested keys ipmideck writes to `config.yaml`.
Environment-variable overrides use a separate `IPMIDECK_` prefix and never appear inside
the YAML file itself.

Whether the login is on is not set here: you switch it from the Security settings, and the
answer is kept in the database, so write access to `config.yaml` cannot turn the login off.

A few optional keys are not written by default. Add them when you need them:

| Key | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `server.cert_file`, `server.key_file` | Your own certificate for `https: true`. Without them ipmideck creates a self-signed one. |
| `server.forwarded_allow_ips` | Behind a reverse proxy: the proxy addresses allowed to set `X-Forwarded-*` headers. |
| `server.trusted_origins` | Behind a reverse proxy that does not pass the browser's `Host`: the external addresses of the dashboard. |
| `ipmi.auto_install_ipmitool` | Let the web UI install ipmitool when it is missing (default `false`). See [Installing ipmitool from the web UI](#installing-ipmitool-from-the-web-ui). |
| `updates.watchtower_url`, `updates.watchtower_token` | Docker only: the Watchtower that installs updates. See [Updating from the web UI](/en/update-from-web-ui#docker-with-watchtower). |

## Environment overrides

Every setting can be overridden at runtime with an `IPMIDECK_`-prefixed environment
variable. This is the easiest way to configure ipmideck in Docker, where you do not want
to edit a file inside the container.

| Environment variable | Description |
|----------------------|-------------|
| `IPMIDECK_SERVER_HOST` | Host/interface the dashboard binds to (default `0.0.0.0`). |
| `IPMIDECK_SERVER_PORT` | HTTP port the dashboard binds to (default `3000`). |
| `IPMIDECK_SERVER_HTTPS` | Serve over HTTPS (default `false`). |
| `IPMIDECK_SERVER_CERT_FILE`, `IPMIDECK_SERVER_KEY_FILE` | Certificate and key for HTTPS. |
| `IPMIDECK_SERVER_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` | Proxy addresses allowed to set `X-Forwarded-*` headers. |
| `IPMIDECK_SERVER_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` | External addresses of the dashboard, separated by commas. |
| `IPMIDECK_AUTH_SESSION_EXPIRY` | How long a login session stays valid (default `24h`). |
| `IPMIDECK_IPMI_POLL_INTERVAL` | Seconds between BMC sensor polls (default `30`). |
| `IPMIDECK_IPMI_POWER_POLL_INTERVAL` | Seconds between power-status polls (default `30`). |
| `IPMIDECK_IPMI_AUTO_INSTALL_IPMITOOL` | Let the web UI install ipmitool when it is missing (default `false`). |
| `IPMIDECK_DATA_RETENTION_DAYS` | Days of sensor history to keep before cleanup (default `365`). |
| `IPMIDECK_DATA_DB_PATH` | Absolute path to the SQLite database file. |
| `IPMIDECK_LOGGING_LEVEL` | Log verbosity: `debug`, `info`, `warning`, or `error` (default `info`). |
| `IPMIDECK_UPDATES_ENABLED` | Set to `false` to switch the update check off completely (default `true`). |
| `IPMIDECK_UPDATES_WATCHTOWER_URL`, `IPMIDECK_UPDATES_WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` | Docker only: address and token of the Watchtower that installs updates. |
| `IPMIDECK_DEMO` | Run against simulated hardware instead of real BMCs (default `false`). |

Two more variables control file *locations* rather than a `config.yaml` value:
`IPMIDECK_DATA_DIR` (the data directory, see below) and `IPMIDECK_CONFIG_PATH` (an
explicit path to a `config.yaml` to load).

<Note>
  Environment variables take precedence over values in `config.yaml`. Set them in your
  `docker run` command (`-e IPMIDECK_SERVER_PORT=8080`) or your `docker-compose.yml`.
</Note>

## Where config lives

ipmideck resolves its data directory from `IPMIDECK_DATA_DIR` if set, otherwise it falls
back to a platform default. `config.yaml` always lives at `<data-dir>/config.yaml`:

- **Docker:** `/data/config.yaml`: the image sets `IPMIDECK_DATA_DIR=/data`; persist
  `/data` with a volume.
- **pip on Linux:** `/data/config.yaml` by default: set `IPMIDECK_DATA_DIR` to relocate it.
- **pip on Windows:** `./data/config.yaml`, relative to the directory you run `ipmideck` from.

## Update checks

ipmideck can tell you when a newer version has been published. First-run setup asks once
whether it may check, and you can change the answer at any time under
**Settings → About → Updates**.

- **What it sends.** One `GET` to the index that matches how you installed: the Python
  package index, the container registry, or the published releases. It carries the product
  name and the version you run, and nothing else: no identifier, no hostname, nothing about
  your servers. When the package index or the container registry reports a newer version, a
  second `GET` asks the published releases whether it is a security release. Every request is written to the log before it is sent.
- **When.** At start-up and once every 24 hours while the check is on, and whenever you
  press **Check now** in Settings or `g` in the [console](/en/console#g-update).
- **What it never does.** The check does not download or install anything. Installing is a
  separate step you start yourself: see [Updating from the web UI](/en/update-from-web-ui).

To switch it off completely, set `updates.enabled: false` in `config.yaml`, or
`IPMIDECK_UPDATES_ENABLED=false`. With that set, ipmideck never opens a connection to look
up a version, whatever was answered during setup, and **Check now** and `g` are refused.

## Installing ipmitool from the web UI

ipmideck reaches every BMC through the `ipmitool` program. When it is missing, ipmideck still
starts, and the web UI shows a banner with the command that installs it on your system.

The banner can also run that command for you, through the system package manager, when all
of these are true:

- `ipmi.auto_install_ipmitool` is `true` (it is `false` by default);
- ipmideck runs as root, or as a user with `sudo` that does not ask for a password;
- the login is on.

ipmideck never asks for a password in the browser. In Docker the image already includes
ipmitool. On Windows there is no package to install: install a tool that ships
`ipmitool.exe`, such as Dell iDRAC Tools, or put `ipmitool.exe` on `PATH`.
